name: Malchiel
overview: Malchiel was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified as the son of Beriah. He is noted among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the early Israelite family migration. His descendants are known as the Malchielites, as mentioned in the book of Numbers.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchiel means 'G-d [El] is [my] king,' reflecting a declaration of divine sovereignty. This proper name, recorded in Genesis, does not indicate it was given directly by God but reveals the theological emphasis present in Israelite naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Malchiel as the son of Beriah. Additionally, he is noted as the father of Birzaith, establishing a direct generational link within the tribe of Asher. These relationships situate him within the genealogical framework of Israel's descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Malchiel's significance lies in his role as an ancestor within the tribe of Asher, contributing to the lineage that journeyed to Egypt and later formed part of the Israelite nation. The mention of the Malchielites in Numbers indicates that his descendants maintained a distinct identity among the tribes, underscoring the importance of genealogical records in preserving Israel's heritage and God's covenant promises.
